attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to route between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3) using an Ansible playbook run from node4 (control_node). Statically addressed node1's eth1 (10.50.10.254/24) and eth2 (10.50.20.254/24) via VyOS configure/commit/save, statically addressed node2's enp8s0 (10.50.10.11/24) and node3's enp8s0 (10.50.20.12/24) via nmcli, added static routes on node2/node3 pointing to node1 for the peer subnet, and trusted the peer subnet in firewalld so any port is reachable. Verified with ping and TCP (HTTP) traffic in both directions, using tcpdump to confirm source IPs are preserved end-to-end (no NAT/masquerade). Bootstrapped SSH access for Ansible using the cluster SSH keypair (added to VyOS user 'vyos' and root on node2/node3; node4 uses the cluster private key). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all four nodes sequentially, confirming changed boot_id and full recovery of routing/connectivity/ansible tooling after each restart.
